Somerville.narrative: Somerville's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,260,000 and every single listing selling above asking price — a 103.8% sale-to-list ratio that underscores just how aggressively buyers are competing for the city's limited inventory. The condo market, the most active segment with 32 sales in the past 30 days, saw a median of $824,950 with a third of units closing over list price, while multi-families led in median price at $1,360,000 with over a third also exceeding asking. With essentially no measurable months of supply across all categories, sellers are in an exceptionally strong position and can realistically expect multiple offers and swift closings. Buyers, particularly those targeting single-families, should come prepared with pre-approval letters, escalation clauses, and a willingness to move quickly, as hesitation in this market almost certainly means losing out.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most fiercely competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes closing at a median of $1,764,000 and condos at $1,005,000 — and with supply so constrained that months of inventory is effectively zero across all property types. The multi-family segment is particularly telling: a median sale price of $1,800,000, a staggering 109.1% sale-to-list ratio, and 75% of homes selling over asking price signal that investors and owner-occupants alike are trading aggressively for the city's limited two- and three-family stock. Even condos, with 51 sales in the past 30 days, are landing exactly at list price on the median with over a third going above ask, meaning buyers should expect to compete with clean, at-or-above-ask offers and minimal contingencies. For sellers, this is about as strong a positioning as the market offers — pricing strategically at or just below market value continues to drive multiple-offer scenarios and strong premiums.

Milton.narrative: Milton's real estate market is showing extraordinary strength across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,150,000 and 39% of properties selling above asking price at a 99% sale-to-list ratio — a clear signal of persistent buyer demand in this highly coveted suburb. Multi-family properties are the standout story, with a median sale price of $1,277,554 and a remarkable 50% of sales closing over asking, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant competition for income-producing assets in the town. Condo buyers are finding slightly less friction, with a median of $725,000 and 25% selling over ask, though a 99.7% SP/LP ratio leaves little room for negotiation there either. With effectively zero months of supply across all categories and 23 single-family homes moving in just the last 30 days, sellers hold an undeniable advantage — serious buyers should come pre-approved, move decisively, and expect to compete aggressively to land a home in Milton's unforgiving market.

Quincy.narrative: Quincy's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes closing at a median of $775,000 and condos at $484,000 — both hitting exactly 100% of list price on average, while multi-families are surging even higher at 104.6% of asking with a median of $825,000. The competition is fierce across all property types, with 60% of multi-families, 45.5% of single-families, and 30% of condos selling above list price, and inventory so tight that months of supply is essentially nonexistent. For sellers, this is an exceptional moment to list, as strong demand and minimal competition virtually guarantee full-price or better offers within a short window. Buyers should be prepared to move decisively, come in with strong financing, and expect to compete — particularly on multi-families, where bidding wars are the clear norm rather than the exception.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with the single-family segment leading the charge — the lone home sold in the past 30 days fetched a median of $750,000 at 107.2% of list price, meaning buyers paid well above asking on every single transaction. Condos are the most active segment with 16 closings, a median sale price of $552,500 at exactly list price, though nearly 44% of units still sold over ask, signaling that well-priced condos continue to attract multiple offers. Multi-families commanded a robust $1,100,000 median despite a slightly softer 95.7% SP/LP ratio, with 14.3% of the 7 sales closing above asking — a sign that investor-grade product is moving, but buyers have a touch more negotiating room. With no measurable months of supply across all categories, sellers hold undeniable leverage, while buyers — particularly those targeting single-family homes — should expect bidding wars and come prepared with strong pre-approvals and escalation clauses from the start.

Medford.narrative: Medford's housing market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes hitting a median sale price of $1,037,500 and selling at exactly list price on average — while 44% of those homes fetched above asking, signaling that well-priced listings are sparking bidding wars. The multi-family segment is arguably the hottest of all, with a striking 105.5% sale-to-list ratio and every single one of the 2 homes sold in the past 30 days closing above asking price at a median of $932,500, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand. Condos offer a comparatively softer entry point at a $719,250 median with a 98.4% sale-to-list ratio, though 22% still sold over ask, meaning buyers can't afford to lowball even in that segment. With essentially zero months of supply across the board, sellers hold enormous leverage right now, and buyers should be prepared to move quickly, waive contingencies strategically, and come in at or above list price to have any realistic chance of winning in Medford.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose continues to demonstrate exceptional demand across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $886,500 and selling at a striking 110.3% of list price — meaning buyers are routinely paying tens of thousands over asking, with three out of four homes going above list price in the last 30 days. The multi-family segment is equally competitive, with a median sale price of $1,110,000 and 66.7% of properties exceeding asking price, while condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at $430,000, though even that segment is selling right at list with 40% closing above ask. With effectively zero months of supply across every category and only 20 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is extremely tight, signaling a deeply undersupplied market. Sellers are in a commanding position and should expect strong offers quickly, while buyers need to come prepared with aggressive financing, clean terms, and a willingness to waive contingencies to have any realistic chance of competing.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,235,000 and closing at 99.6% of list price, while a striking 40% of those 20 sales in the past 30 days went above asking. Multi-family properties are the hottest segment of all, with 60% selling over list price and a median sale-to-list ratio of 104.8%, pushing the median to $1,106,000 — a clear signal that investors and house-hackers are aggressively chasing Arlington's rental income potential. Condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at a $735,000 median, though with 26.7% still closing above ask and virtually no measurable months of supply across all categories, buyers should expect multiple-offer situations and need to come prepared with strong financials and competitive terms. For sellers, this is an exceptional moment to list — lean inventory means minimal competition and strong leverage, particularly for those with multi-family assets or well-positioned single-family homes.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,552,500 and closing at 98.6% of list price, while a remarkable 37.5% of those homes sold above asking — a clear signal that well-priced properties are still generating competitive offers. The condo market is equally tight, with a $1,257,500 median and half of all units selling over list price, and the multi-family segment is the most heated of all, with 100% of sales exceeding ask and a jaw-dropping 105.8% sale-to-list ratio on a $1,375,000 median. With effectively zero months of supply across all property types and only 13 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is critically constrained, making this an exceptionally strong seller's market. Buyers should expect to move quickly, come in at or above list price with minimal contingencies, and be prepared for stiff competition — particularly on multi-families, where investors and owner-occupants alike are aggressively chasing limited opportunities in this coveted suburb.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's real estate market is operating at a fever pitch, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $2,225,000 and selling at 97.3% of list price, with more than a third of transactions closing above asking — a clear signal that well-priced homes are attracting multiple offers fast. The condo market is even more competitive, with a median sale price of $1,160,000 and an average sale-to-list ratio of 100.4%, meaning buyers are routinely paying over asking price, as evidenced by 60% of condos selling above list in the past 30 days. With effectively zero months of supply across all property types, Winchester is deeply entrenched in seller's market territory, giving homeowners exceptional leverage and the realistic expectation of strong, swift offers. For buyers, this environment demands preparation — financing locked in, decisions made quickly, and offers structured aggressively — as hesitation in Winchester almost certainly means losing out to competing bids.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes hitting a median sale price of $1,000,000 and selling at exactly list price on average, while an impressive 36.4% of those homes closed above asking — a clear signal that well-priced properties are drawing multiple offers. The condo market, the most active segment with 306 sales in the past 30 days, posted a median of $766,250 with nearly 1 in 5 units selling over ask, while multi-families led in median price at $1,150,000, with 32.6% selling above list despite a slight 2.1% average concession from list price. With inventory so tight that months of supply is essentially unmeasurable across all categories, sellers hold strong negotiating leverage and can expect swift, competitive offers — especially for single-family and multi-family properties. Buyers should come prepared with pre-approvals in hand, escalation clauses at the ready, and realistic expectations that the asking price is often just the starting point in Boston's unyielding market.
